passages.citationLabel: On the Genealogy of Morality, Preface §§3–6
passages.interpretiveNote: Moral values have histories and must themselves be evaluated by asking what conditions produced them and whether they enhance or diminish life.

passages.citationLabel: On the Genealogy of Morality, First Essay §§10–11
passages.interpretiveNote: Slave morality's opposition of evil and good grows reactively from ressentiment and reverses an earlier noble valuation.
